questions.question: What determines the set of values an object can have and the operations that can be performed on it?
questions.explanation: An object's type defines the range of values it may hold and which operations are permitted. (Source Page: [1])

questions.question: Which standard header defines symbolic constants for the sizes of integer types?
questions.explanation: <limits.h> contains the symbolic constants for integer type sizes. (Source Page: [2])

questions.question: Which standard header provides symbolic constants related to floating‑point properties?
questions.explanation: <float.h> defines the floating‑point limits and related constants. (Source Page: [2])

questions.question: According to the ANSI C standard, which statement about integer types is correct?

options.C: Both signed and unsigned forms exist for all integer types.

questions.explanation: The ANSI standard adds signed and unsigned forms for every integer type. (Source Page: [1])

questions.question: What effect does declaring an object with the qualifier `const` have?

options.A: It allows the object to be modified freely.
options.B: It prevents the object from being changed after initialization.
options.C: It forces the object to be stored in read‑only memory.
options.D: It makes the object invisible to other translation units.

questions.explanation: `const` objects cannot be altered once defined. (Source Page: [1])

questions.question: How many characters of an internal identifier are guaranteed to be significant in C?
questions.explanation: At least the first 31 characters of an internal name are significant. (Source Page: [1])

questions.question: For external names, the C standard guarantees uniqueness for how many characters?
questions.explanation: Uniqueness for external names is guaranteed only for the first 6 characters (case‑insensitive). (Source Page: [1])

questions.question: Which of the following can be concatenated automatically at compile time?
questions.explanation: The language permits compile‑time concatenation of string constants. (Source Page: [1])

questions.question: Which type provides extended precision beyond the standard double type?
questions.explanation: The `long double` type offers extended precision. (Source Page: [1])

questions.question: The rules for automatic coercions among arithmetic types have been augmented to handle what?
questions.explanation: The coercion rules now cover the richer set of arithmetic types introduced by the ANSI changes. (Source Page: [1])
